points.label: Local payroll complexity
points.text: Australian higher education gives the practice a concrete reference: Federation University combines HCM and Payroll delivery with later compliance and platform enhancements.

points.label: Boutique roots, global ownership
points.text: Part of the ANZ lineage runs through Duane Goff and Mark Ohlin’s Theory of Mind: acquired by Collaborative in 2018, then incorporated into Cognizant through the 2020 acquisition.

points.label: Evidence beyond go-live
points.text: Federation’s TAFE EBA work is a useful payroll-complexity reference. Finance and Student remain future phases in that case; verify the proposed team’s continuity with the demonstrated work.

points.label: A local practice taking shape
points.text: Kainos’s FY26 report describes ANZ growth from a small base and names Perth Airport. GO membership adds a mid-market route alongside its enterprise work.

points.label: Built through regional people
points.text: Mitch Collins brings a documented Cognizant and Australian Payroll history. Regional Adaptive and payroll appointments show how Kainos is assembling expertise, with APAC scope retained.

points.label: Separate delivery from hiring
points.text: Perth Airport has a delivery-leader account of HCM and recruitment go-live. The Adaptive and payroll appointments are capability signals; local customer outcomes for those domains still need establishing here.

points.label: A newer route into Workday
points.text: Kliqtek combines advisory, project delivery, support and resourcing with GO participation. Its proposition centres on helping smaller organisations adopt and operate Workday.

points.label: Repeat founders, shared delivery
points.text: Dougall and Trish McBurnie founded Kliqtek in 2024 after Versor and Fujitsu. The Kliqxe joint venture adds enterprise-platform experience; the founders’ earlier company-building record is distinct from Workday delivery.

points.label: Early evidence, bounded claims
points.text: An anonymous manufacturing client describes Workday-related HR work across Australia, New Zealand and the UK. A named customer, precise delivery scope and repeat support outcomes would make the local practice easier to assess.

points.label: Planning beside another ERP
points.text: Fusion5’s differentiator is visible in AFL’s design: Adaptive Planning alongside Dynamics 365 finance, with integration and separate reporting environments for clubs. That is a concrete planning proposition.

points.label: A regional applications business
points.text: Founded in 2003 and now BGH-backed, Fusion5 brings a wider applications business to Workday planning. The AFL rollout dates to 2022; unrelated group acquisitions should not stand in for Workday depth.

points.label: A named multi-entity rollout
points.text: AFL, 13 clubs and two related entities establish Adaptive implementation and integration experience. They do not establish delivery of Workday’s core Financial Management or HCM products.

points.label: Support becoming deployment
points.text: Mivada is expanding from Workday support into GO deployment. That creates a useful proposition to test: whether experience operating customers’ systems improves how it implements new ones.

points.label: An established support base
points.text: The company dates its founding to 2014, India delivery centre to 2018 and Workday AMS launch to 2019. Its team names Rama Madivada and program/payroll leader Laura Zlendich.

points.label: A build under way
points.text: Workday’s May 2026 launch quotes Mivada building its deployment practice and adopting GO itself. That substantiates commitment and direction; a named external deployment would demonstrate the expanded delivery model.

points.label: Support for the customer’s side
points.text: CloudRock spans readiness, implementation support, optimisation and AMS. The useful distinction is its role alongside a transformation programme: establish what it owns and what remains with the deployment partner.

points.label: Two specialist businesses combine
points.text: Founder Minos Ataliotis’s CloudRock acquired Bas Eggelaar’s SuccessDay in January 2026. SuccessDay retains its brand and leadership, adding European advisory and AMS experience to the group.

points.label: Presence precedes local proof
points.text: Australia is in CloudRock’s footprint, and its APAC team appeared at Workday Elevate Sydney. Named Australian engagements and team continuity would establish how the enlarged group’s capability reaches local customers.

points.label: Specialist lineage with operating reach
points.text: Fujitsu combines Enable’s regional ServiceNow specialism with a larger integration and operations business. AEMO gives the enterprise workflow and risk proposition a named Australian reference.

points.label: Enable is the relevant inheritance
points.text: Enable, founded in 2014, joined Fujitsu in 2022. Bruce Hara was its CEO at the announcement; that historical leadership explains the acquired practice without establishing today’s delivery team.

points.label: An Australian enterprise platform
points.text: AEMO’s case describes Fujitsu implementing a ServiceNow platform with centralised risk and automated workflows. Ask which proposed practitioners carry that experience and which ongoing responsibilities the supplier will own.

points.label: A regional specialist inside RGP
points.text: CloudGo supplies the relevant APAC ServiceNow lineage within RGP’s broader consulting business. Its continuing corporate profile offers workflow consulting from an Australia and Singapore base.

points.label: Built before the parent arrived
points.text: Rahul Garg and Rory Fitzpatrick founded CloudGo in 2016. RGP completed its acquisition in November 2023 to combine it with Veracity and expand digital consulting across APAC.

points.label: Verify the continuing practice
points.text: The sources establish the regional business and current offer, but no named ANZ engagement is captured here. Validate the actual team and scope; the sale-era employee figure covered the region, not Australia alone.

engagementClaims.text: Cognizant’s Federation University case explicitly describes completed Workday HCM and Payroll go-live, followed by payroll configuration, testing and deployment work for a new TAFE EBA.
engagementClaims.dateLabel: Undated case; go-live and subsequent work described retrospectively
engagementClaims.limit: Evidence of this Australian Payroll engagement, not every payroll module or the current availability of its delivery team. Finance and Student are future phases in the source.

engagementClaims.text: Fusion5 says it rolled out Workday Adaptive Planning in 2022 for AFL, 13 clubs and two related entities, integrated with Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations.
engagementClaims.limit: Adaptive implementation and integration beside Microsoft finance; not Workday Financial Management implementation.

engagementClaims.text: Fujitsu’s AEMO case states that the partners implemented an integrated ServiceNow enterprise platform and describes centralised risk data and automated workflows.
engagementClaims.limit: Broad risk-workflow implementation evidence. The page does not establish a specific IRM or Security Operations SKU, an exact go-live date, or current staffing.
